title: Handler inventory: request-to-reply formal coverage per HTTP route
author: vela-h1-handlers

corpus.additional_routers: none: lib.rs has no router; main.rs only adds RequestBodyLimitLayer + TimeoutLayer to routes::build
corpus.fallback: SPA fallback_service when WEB_DIR is set (routes.rs:232-240), not an API route and not counted
corpus.correspondence: security/formal/correspondence.json is drift-detection snapshots of protocol/client artifacts, not a route map; it has no per-route entry

verdict_definitions.driver+interpreter+executors proved: the handler reaches a policy driver only through that crate's proved interpreter macro (or an equivalent proved loop), and every SQL/store operation in the request is an extracted plan proved against the store model
verdict_definitions.partially proved: at least the store statements are extracted plans with a store-model proof, but at least one part named in the row is ordinary handler code (usually: no decision driver at all, or a write whose authority is an inline branch)
verdict_definitions.no proof (read-only): no driver and no proved statement I/O; the route only reads (or probes) and its reply cannot change security state
verdict_definitions.no proof (writes): a route that writes with neither a proved decision loop nor proved statement I/O

global_middleware: CORS allow-list or wildcard-if-explicitly-allowed, exposes X-New-Token (routes.rs:36-60)
security_headers: nosniff, DENY, no-referrer, CSP, HSTS when HTTPS (routes.rs:248, 255-296)
AuthSession: PASETO verify, exp/nbf/hard-cap, revocation markers + durable device row, 300 req/min per JTI, verified renewal (middleware.rs:78-241)
DeviceSession: AuthSession + authorize_route(PermanentAccount) refusing web-session scope (middleware.rs:300-323)

routes.io: `RegisterIo` (session-executors): rate limit, account count, begin, insert user, insert device, commit, issue token, track JTI. No SQL outside plans.
routes.reply: `RegisterResponse{user_id, device_id, token}` on `Complete`; `registration_failure_error` (account/mod.rs:348) maps each driver failure to 429/400/500; unmatched effect = 500. Errors render through `AppError` (error.rs:46).

routes.reply: `{"deleted":true,"user_id":...}` on `Complete`; failure branches keep the recorded store error, else `deletion_failure_error`; unmatched = 500.
